item.title: Why Yoro’s red card against Liverpool was overturned – FA panel
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Football Association has released the written reasons for overturning Leny Yoro’s red card for Manchester United against Liverpool, despite refereeing body Pro Ref maintaining that the on-field decision was not clearly wrong. According to Sky Sports, the FA’s independent regulatory commission unanimously ruled that referee Sam Barrott made an “obvious error” in deciding Liverpool striker Alexander Isak had an obvious goalscoring opportunity when Yoro fouled him during United’s 4-0 defeat at Anfield on Sunday. The panel said Isak’s touch was so heavy that he had lost control of the ball, allowing United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to close in and potentially gather it before the striker could shoot. “Taking the foul committed by Yoro out of the scenario, Isak would not have had an obvious goalscoring opportunity,” the commission said in its written reasons. The decision overturned Yoro’s one-match suspension, making the defender available for United’s Premier League match against Brentford on Saturday. Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb had defended the officials’ decision, saying Isak was moving quickly towards the ball and that it was “certainly not clearly wrong” to judge he would reach it before Lammens. United submitted video evidence from several angles, as well as footage of Brighton defender Pascal Struijk’s red card against Sunderland, which was overturned after an appeal. The club also argued that Isak would have been at least 1.8 metres short of the ball without Yoro’s challenge. The commission said it could not test the validity of United’s distance analysis and therefore viewed it with caution. A separate Premier League Key Match Incidents panel is reported to have backed the original decision; its findings for the matchweek are due to be published on December 2. item.title: 2027 election: Atiku, Amaechi have best experience in governance — Dele Momodu
item.description: The Deputy Director-General, Media and Communication of the African Democratic Congress, Dele Momodu, has described former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and former Rivers State Governor Rotimi Amaechi as politicians with the best experience in governance ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Momodu said the duo had the experience and capacity to tackle Nigeria’s challenges, expressing confidence that Atiku could revive moribund industries, including the Ajaokuta Steel Company, by engaging competent professionals. He spoke in an interview on Trust TV on Thursday, while defending Atiku’s ability to deliver on his promises if elected president in 2027. Momodu said he believed in Atiku’s leadership ability, citing his success in business and willingness to deploy expertise in addressing difficult national challenges. “Nothing is impossible with the determination of a leader, and I know Alhaji Atiku Abubakar to be a very different kind of leader, and that’s why he’s been able to run his own business successfully,” he said. The ADC chieftain said Atiku’s promise to revamp the Ajaokuta Steel Company should not be interpreted as a plan to repeat past approaches, but as an opportunity to bring in professionals with the requisite expertise to restore the facility. “If he tells you that he will revamp Ajaokuta, it does not mean that he will do it the way they did it decades ago. He will bring in the best expert,” Momodu said. He cited the revival of Nigeria’s railway system under the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari as an example of how leadership and competent personnel could transform infrastructure previously considered beyond recovery. Momodu credited Amaechi, who served as Minister of Transportation under Buhari, with delivering railway projects that restored public confidence in train transportation across parts of the country. “You can see even while President Buhari was in power, there was a man who was able to do and deliver so many projects, and that man is the Right Honourable Chibuke Rotimi Amaechi,” he said. According to Momodu, Nigerians had previously lost hope in the railway system but became proud of the trains following the projects executed during Amaechi’s tenure. “People gave up on our trains, that the railways will never function again in Nigeria. But you can see within a short time, we were all very proud to show off our trains as they moved in different parts of Nigeria,” he said. He expressed optimism that a combination of Atiku’s experience and Amaechi’s record in infrastructure development would deliver better governance if they worked together in 2027. “So the same thing will happen if you bring in Atiku Amaechi together in 2027. These guys have the best experience in governance,” Momodu added. The post 2027 election: Atiku, Amaechi have best experience in governance — Dele Momodu appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nathaniel Bassey builds subsidised apartments for staff, musicians
item.description: Gospel singer Nathaniel Bassey has revealed that he has built apartments for his staff and musicians under a housing scheme designed to help them become homeowners. The singer disclosed this in an Instagram post, where he shared his excitement about seeing the beneficiaries move into their homes with their families by Christmas. Bassey said the project, which he named Love Song Apartments, was driven by his long-standing desire to help members of his team own houses. He explained that the housing scheme required the beneficiaries to contribute a significant portion of the cost, while the apartments were offered to them at highly subsidised rates. According to him, he provided a family-owned plot of land and contributed funds towards the project, while his friend, Peter Chubby of Danville Mall, partnered with him through a joint venture arrangement. The singer said construction began gradually, with the team building the apartments in phases. “One thing I realised doing this was that we used to be told musicians were not organised. But with the right guidance, they can do great things. They have committed to this. See, you never know what you can do until you try,” he wrote. Bassey said he was particularly delighted at the prospect of seeing the beneficiaries settle into their fully owned apartments with their children enjoying the play area provided within the estate. He described the project as an expression of his belief that leadership should involve extending opportunities and blessings to others. “This is never to brag. I’m not that kind of person. But sometimes, people need to see these things to know God is faithful,” he added. The singer also disclosed that the housing project was only its first phase, expressing hope that more apartments would be developed in the future. He said he hoped to share the knowledge and experience gained from the initiative with other creatives and musicians in the Christian community to encourage them to pursue similar projects. Bassey further emphasised the importance of leaders carrying their team members along as they achieve personal success, saying that a leader should not be the only one enjoying the benefits of progress. “Finally, as a leader, if you are the only one sharing testimonies, after a while, those around you will soon be despondent. Make sure as God lifts you, you carry them along,” he wrote. The post Nathaniel Bassey builds subsidised apartments for staff, musicians appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mock Accreditation: INEC Faces Crucial Test As 100 Million Voters Await 2027 Elections
item.description: With exactly 50 days before Nigerians return to the ballot, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is preparing for a nationwide test that could offer an important indication of whether the country is ready for another fiercely contested general election. On Saturday, November 28, the electoral umpire will deploy its Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and electronic results upload technology across 17,676 selected polling units in a mock exercise designed to identify operational weaknesses, test equipment reliability and strengthen public confidence ahead of the 2027 elections. The exercise, scheduled for 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., will cover two polling units in each of the country’s 8,838 registration areas, giving INEC an opportunity to assess the performance of its electoral technology across different locations before the presidential and National Assembly elections on January 16, 2027, and the governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections on February 6. #OsunDecides2026: Election Officers Take Delivery Of Materials, Mobilise To Polling Units during the Osun State governorship election on August 15, 2026. It comes against the backdrop of lingering controversies surrounding the 2023 general elections, particularly the failure to upload presidential election results to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) in real time, technical difficulties associated with BVAS and allegations of electoral irregularities. Chairman of INEC, Joash Amupitan, described the mock exercise as an important part of preparations for the forthcoming elections, while urging Nigerians to participate. The commission’s Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Victoria Meci, explained that the exercise would allow INEC to establish the effectiveness and reliability of its equipment before election day. “We don’t want to wait till the elections before we test the ruggedness, readiness and functionality of the system,” she said during an appearance on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily . According to her, the commission has reduced the accreditation threshold to 850 voters per BVAS device, with additional machines to be provided at polling units with larger voter populations. The exercise will also test the electronic upload of results to IReV, although Meci acknowledged that successful transmission would depend on network availability. 100 Million Voters, 176,846 Polling Units The scale of the preparations reflects the size of Nigeria’s electorate. INEC says it is now managing a verified national register of more than 100 million voters after removing over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated, and deceased records from the previous register of approximately 103 million. Amupitan disclosed on Wednesday, during a meeting with resident electoral commissioners from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, that the clean-up followed the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System and a statutory claims-and-objections audit. item.title: FG targets $200m trade with Tunisia by 2028
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has proposed a $200 million bilateral trade target with Tunisia by 2028 and supported moves to establish direct flights between both countries to boost trade, tourism and people-to-people relations. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Sola Enikanolaiye, made the proposal when Tunisia’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Antit Moshen, visited him in Abuja on Tuesday. In a statement on Thursday, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said Enikanolaiye identified direct air connectivity as a key factor in strengthening economic and diplomatic relations between the two countries. He said direct flights would facilitate trade and tourism, promote educational exchanges and strengthen ties between Nigerians and Tunisians. The minister also called for greater private-sector participation in bilateral economic relations, urging Nigerian companies, including the Dangote Group, to explore investment opportunities in Tunisia. Speaking during the meeting, Moshen disclosed that bilateral trade between Nigeria and Tunisia had increased from $7 million to more than $100 million by 2024. He identified the absence of direct flights as a major obstacle to deeper bilateral relations, assuring that Tunisia was committed to addressing the challenge. The Tunisian ambassador also reaffirmed his country’s commitment to maintaining its annual scholarship allocation for Nigerian students. In response, Enikanolaiye said he would work with relevant government institutions to facilitate access to the scholarship opportunities for eligible Nigerians. He also called for increased cooperation between both countries in French-language education. The minister further expressed Nigeria’s readiness to work towards convening the sixth session of the Nigeria–Tunisia Joint Commission in the first quarter of 2027. He said the meeting would provide an opportunity for both countries to review their bilateral relations, strengthen cooperation and address outstanding issues. item.title: Senate probes LPG exports over domestic supply shortage
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has raised concerns over inadequate supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) to the domestic market, warning that the shortfall could undermine efforts to reduce the price of cooking gas in the country. The Senate Committee on Gas Resources, chaired by Senator Jarigbe Jarigbe (APC, Cross River North), raised the concern on Thursday during an interface with stakeholders in the gas sector on export revenue remittances and domestic LPG supply. The meeting, held at the National Assembly complex, Abuja, was convened to examine the availability of LPG in the domestic market, export volumes and revenue remittances from the country’s gas sector. Jarigbe said the situation was contrary to the objectives of Presidential Executive Order 9, signed by President Bola Tinubu on February 13, 2026, which seeks to improve oil and gas revenue remittances to the Federation Account. He said the government also needed to ensure adequate domestic gas supply to reduce the financial burden on Nigerians. “LPG has to be supplied to the domestic market for the good of the common man as intended with Executive Order 9 issued by President Tinubu to ameliorate the sufferings of the masses on price of gas,” he said. The executive order, however, focuses primarily on oil and gas revenue remittances rather than expressly mandating domestic LPG supply. Speaking to journalists after the meeting, the lawmaker said the committee was determined to establish the reasons for the inadequate supply and work towards bringing down cooking gas prices. “We are already working for Nigerians here, for our people, and that’s why we want to get to the root of it. “And we’ll make sure that the price of gas goes down, because when there is adequate supply in response to demand, the price will naturally go down,” he said. Jarigbe said industry operators had attributed the export of some LPG to the ratio of propane to butane in the product. He, however, argued that the composition could be adjusted through blending to make more of the product suitable for domestic consumption. “They give an excuse that the ratio of propane to butane is 80-20, and that’s what they export. But it’s a matter of blending, so that it will be the reverse: the quantity of butane will be 80 per cent, while the quantity of propane will be 20 per cent for local consumption in Nigeria,” he said. During the meeting, the Deputy Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Customs Service in charge of Tariff and Trade, Caroline Kemen Niagwan, presented the agency’s records of LPG exports. Niagwan said 190.8 metric tonnes of LPG were exported in 2024, while 32.8 metric tonnes were recorded in 2025, bringing the cumulative volume for the two years to 223.699 metric tonnes. “The summary is that a total of 190.8 metric tonnes of LPG was exported in 2024. item.title: FG urges South Korean firms to establish factories
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has urged major South Korean companies to establish manufacturing and assembly plants in Nigeria as part of efforts to create jobs, boost local production and strengthen the country’s industrial capacity. The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Sola Enikanolaiye, made the appeal when South Korea’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Jeong Yo-an, visited him in Abuja on Tuesday. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs disclosed this in a statement on Thursday. Enikanolaiye said the presence of South Korean brands, including LG, Kia and Samsung, in Nigeria reflected the growing trade relations between both countries. He urged the companies to build on the existing relationship by establishing factories and operational offices in Nigeria, citing the country’s young and skilled workforce. The minister also called for increased South Korean investment in agriculture, solid minerals, manufacturing and the marine economy. In his response, Jeong identified technology transfer, industrial development and agriculture as areas with significant potential for closer cooperation between the two countries. He said South Korea was ready to share its development experience with Nigeria to support the country’s industrial growth. The two sides also discussed plans to hold the seventh session of the Nigeria–Korea Joint Commission in the first quarter of 2027. They further emphasised the need to conclude outstanding bilateral agreements, including an agreement on the avoidance of double taxation. item.title: ‘I have no time for anybody’ – Okpebholo denies involvement in NDC Edo attack
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has dismissed allegations linking him to the attack on supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Benin City, saying he has no time for those accusing him. Okpebholo spoke on Thursday at an All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in Ehor, the administrative headquarters of Uhunmwonde Local Government Area, a day after gunmen attacked NDC supporters who had gathered along Airport Road to welcome the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to the state. The governor described the allegations against him as lies, insisting that he did not use thugs during his previous political campaigns. “Yesterday some people were crying because when they thought they would come to Edo and shine, when they got here, they met only three people in the hall. They started shooting themselves because they want to spoil our name. They started calling my name but I have no time for anybody. They are lying,” he said. He added that hearing his name mentioned during a television report made him conclude that the claims being circulated about him were untrue. Okpebholo also denied using thugs during his political campaigns, recalling his contests for the Senate and governorship. “When I was contesting for Senate, I didn’t use thugs. When I was contesting for governor, I did not use thugs,” he said. The governor further claimed that the NDC chairman was among those previously implicated in the killing of his police officer, but said he had refrained from pursuing the matter to avoid accusations of political victimisation. “The NDC chairman was one of those that were fingered at that time. If I start now, they will say that I am victimising them because of politics,” he added. The attack occurred on Wednesday along Airport Road in Benin City, where gunmen reportedly opened fire on people waiting to receive Obi ahead of his town hall meeting in the state. The Edo State Police Command said three gunmen in a black Toyota Hilux opened fire after encountering police operatives stationed at the airport exit gate. One person, identified as Aimionkhale Micheal, sustained gunshot injuries to his thighs and was taken to hospital. The police said Commissioner of Police Patrick Daaor had ordered an investigation and directed tactical operatives to track down the fleeing suspects. The NDC condemned the incident and called for an investigation into the attack. As of Thursday, the police had not publicly identified the suspects or announced any arrests. item.title: Delta attack: PANDEF writes IGP, DSS DG, demands probe
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) has written to the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, and the Director-General of the Department of State Services (DSS), Oluwatosin Ajayi, demanding an urgent investigation into the reported violence at a political rally in Ughelli, Delta State. The socio-political organisation called on both security chiefs to work with other relevant agencies to identify and prosecute those who allegedly planned, sponsored, instigated or participated in the attack on the campaign train of former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Omo-Agege, who is the All Progressives Congress (APC) senatorial candidate for Delta Central, was reportedly attacked during a campaign rally on Monday, November 23, 2026, with some persons said to have been killed and several others injured. In a letter signed by its National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, PANDEF strongly condemned the incident and described the reported loss of lives and injuries as disturbing and unacceptable. The organisation also urged the Federal Government, relevant federal agencies and the Delta State Government to provide financial and other forms of assistance to families of those reportedly killed, as well as adequate medical care for the injured. In the letter, PANDEF said it was shocked by reports of violence at a political rally organised by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in parts of Uduere, Delta State, on Monday. It, however, noted that the reports of deaths and injuries had yet to be officially corroborated. “According to media reports, which are yet to be officially corroborated, some persons reportedly lost their lives, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries. We consider these reported incidents extremely disturbing and totally unacceptable,” the letter stated. PANDEF recalled that it had issued a statement the previous week warning against political violence, intimidation and intolerance of opposition parties in the South-South. It said the latest incident, coming days after its appeal, was a source of grave concern, adding that the region had traditionally upheld political tolerance, sportsmanship and civility. The organisation further warned that insecurity in the South-South could have implications beyond the region, given its strategic importance to Nigeria’s oil and gas industry and national economy. “Any disruption of peace and security in the region, particularly violence associated with political and electoral activities, could have far-reaching implications, not only for the safety and wellbeing of our people but also for the stability and economic survival of the country,” it said. PANDEF urged the police, DSS and other security agencies to conduct a comprehensive, impartial and thorough investigation and ensure that anyone found culpable was brought to justice in accordance with the law. item.title: Tinubu willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists — Bwala
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Special Adviser to the President on Media and Policy Communication, Daniel Bwala, has said President Bola Tinubu is willing to grant more interviews to Nigerian journalists, while maintaining that the Presidency will decide which media organisations interview him. Bwala said this during an interview on the Niger Unfiltered podcast, published on Thursday, following questions about why Tinubu had granted only one official interview to Nigerian media organisations in about three years and seven months in office. “I expect us to do more. And the second time, you’ll see more of that,” Bwala said. He acknowledged that some interviews had been postponed at short notice, saying the President had sometimes agreed to meet journalists before later rescheduling. “There are a number of times in which the President called for media. At the 11th hour, he may have been advised, and then he would apologise and say some other time,” Bwala said. The presidential aide said Tinubu was willing to speak with journalists and did not need prepared answers or prior briefings before interviews. “There is a willingness to grant interviews on the part of the President. And the President, when granting interviews, didn’t need to read anything, didn’t need to be briefed,” he said. Bwala defended the Presidency’s right to choose the journalists and platforms it engages, saying it should not be pressured to grant interviews to specific media organisations. “We control our narrative. We decide who we grant interviews to. Nobody can come and tell us, grant to this one and not the other one,” he said. He said State House press corps members representing mainstream, new, social and print media covered the President’s daily activities. “In the State House press corps, we have representatives of the mainstream, the new media, the social media, and the print media. So every day, the activity of the President is covered by them,” Bwala said. He also criticised some media practitioners over what he described as political bias and a lack of professionalism, arguing that Tinubu should engage journalists capable of conducting balanced interviews. Bwala’s remarks followed criticism of Tinubu’s recent interview with American political strategist and media personality Diana London. Some Nigerians questioned why the President had granted an interview to a foreign media personality while rarely speaking with Nigerian journalists. The controversy grew after reports linked London to a $4.5 million lobbying arrangement involving a United States-based firm engaged by the Nigerian government. London denied receiving the money from the Federal Government or anyone in Nigeria, saying she travelled to Nigeria to interview Tinubu for a documentary. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar also challenged Tinubu to grant a live interview to Nigerian journalists and called for the release of the full, unedited recording of his conversation with London. item.title: FCCPC urges supermarkets to protect consumer trust
item.description: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) has urged supermarket and shopping mall operators across the country to strengthen consumer protection practices and earn customers’ trust through transparent business operations. The Executive Vice Chairman of the commission, Mr Tunji Bello, gave the advice through the Lagos Zonal Coordinator, Dr Olubunmi Otti, at a one-day sectoral roundtable on compliance and enforcement of the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act (FCCPA) 2018, held in Lagos. The engagement, themed, “Compliance Obligations of Supermarket Operators,” was organised to sensitise operators on their responsibilities under the law, particularly as the yuletide shopping season approaches. Bello said supermarkets had become essential to millions of Nigerians, serving as major outlets for purchasing food, medicines, children’s necessities and other household essentials. He said customers placed their health, money and trust in the hands of supermarket operators whenever they patronised their businesses, adding that such trust must be protected. “The supermarket is no longer just a shop for millions of Nigerians; it is where they buy their food, medicine, children’s needs and daily essentials. “When a consumer walks into your store, they are placing their trust, their health and hard-earned money in your hands. That trust must be protected,” he said. The FCCPC boss said the FCCPA 2018 empowered the commission to protect consumers, promote fair competition and ensure that businesses operated transparently and accountably. He said the roundtable focused on the commission’s role in guiding compliance, consumer rights under the Act, safety standards in retail outlets, the legal framework and complaint resolution mechanisms. Bello disclosed that the commission received complaints daily concerning the supermarket sector, including discrepancies between shelf prices and prices charged at checkout points, the sale of expired or nearly expired products without clear disclosure, misleading promotions and discounts, poor refund and return policies, and inadequate product information. He cited the experience of a mother who budgeted N50,000 for monthly shopping but encountered higher prices at the payment counter, describing such discrepancies as a breach of consumer trust rather than a mere mistake. He said the commission’s objective was to reduce and ultimately eliminate such complaints, not to shut down businesses, but to help operators understand and comply with their obligations. “Compliance is not a burden; compliance is good business,” he said, adding that customers who trusted a supermarket’s products and refund policies were more likely to return. The engagement attracted representatives of supermarket and retail businesses, including Justrite Superstores, Jendol Superstores, Prince Ebeano Supermarkets, Sundry Foods and Edichat Pharmacy and Stores. item.title: Igbokoda crash: Tinubu approves N100m, three-bedroom houses for victims’ families
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi President Bola Tinubu has approved three-bedroom flats in Abuja for the families of the 25 people who died in the October 5, 2026 Nigerian Air Force aircraft crash. He also announced the award of the sum of N100 million to the families of each military personnel who died in the crash, separate from the houses. The President made the announcement on Thursday during a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony held in honour of the victims of the NAF ATR 42 aircraft accident. He said the houses, located in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja, would be allocated to the immediate families of the deceased military personnel and civilians who were aboard the aircraft. Tinubu described the housing allocation as a demonstration of the nation’s appreciation for the sacrifices of the fallen personnel. “As a tangible expression of the nation’s gratitude, I approve the allocation of three-bedroom flats in the Renewed Hope Housing Project in Abuja to the family of each of the military personnel who lost their lives in this accident. “No home can ever replace the one you have lost, but they gave their lives for Nigeria, and Nigeria will give their family a home,” he said. The president pointed out that the gesture would also be extended to the immediate families of the civilians on board the aircraft. “In addition to the flats, these officers would receive from this government N100m each,” he said. He assured the bereaved families that the government would remain committed to supporting them beyond the memorial ceremony. “Long after the wreaths have faded, our commitment to these families must remain evergreen,” Tinubu said. The president also assured Nigerians that the October 5 aircraft crash would be thoroughly investigated, promising that the findings would inform improvements in military and civilian aviation safety. “I assure the grieving nation that this accident will be thoroughly investigated. We will seek answers. We will learn the lessons. We will strengthen our military and civilian aviation safety standards. Our operational procedures and our institutional accountability will be strengthened. “We owe them the truth, and we will honour that debt,” he said. Tinubu further reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving the welfare, safety and operational capacity of the Armed Forces through modernisation, training and better equipment. “A nation that asks its sons and daughters to fly into danger must give them the best wings it can build,” he added. The president urged the bereaved families to remember the deceased for their service and contributions to the country, assuring them that their sacrifices would remain in the nation’s memory. The October 5 accident claimed the lives of 25 people, including military personnel and civilians. item.title: Kwara Jailbreak: How negligence, insecurity aided inmates’ escape from 112-year-old Ilorin prison
item.description: By Demola Akinyemi, Ilorin The jailbreak at the Correctional Centre, Oke-Kura, Ilorin, Kwara State, in the wee hours of last week Wednesday (November 18, 2026) exposed negligence, compromise of the staff and obsolete security equipment, according to Vanguard investigations. Sources at the centre confided in Vanguard that seven condemned prison inmates actually planned their escape, out of which two – Segun and Abraham – now declared wanted, were lucky. They had been planning their escape for about seven months. The rooms of the condemned prison inmates are said to be secluded and often dark, as they’re not supposed to go out like others. Vanguard also gathered that once in a while, when the condemned inmates go out to do social services, they are always heavily guarded. It was further gathered that for the seven months, they used a chisel to gradually opened the wall of their room, to create enough hole space for them to escape into the premises. Vanguard also gathered that they used posters to cover the space (inside and outside) so that no staff could easily notice their escape plan. It was further gathered that the Correctional Centre fence, about 17 feet high, was topped with embedded broken glass rather than a wire mesh. Furthermore, there is no CCTV camera covering inmates’ movements. D-Day On the day of escape, they got thick blankets which they tied together to make a long thick rope, and hooked it to the broken glasses on top of the fence. It was with this blanket-rope that the condemned inmates climbed over the tall fence and escaped to the other side, said a source. But after Segun and Abraham had scaled the fence, the blanket became weak. So it gave way, and the other five would-be escapees fell back on the prison premises. Vanguard also gathered that fully armed officers of the center, who were supposed to be on 24/7 surveillance to secure the other side of the fence, weren’t there to arrest the condemned inmates. It was during the morning roll call on Wednesday that the Correctional Centre staff on duty discovered that two condemned inmates had escaped. item.title: ‘I bought book on how to have boy-child’ – Makinde
item.description: By Angel Aniobi Oyo State Governor, Seyi Makinde has revealed that he bought a book and ovulation kits with his wife in their attempt to have a male child after welcoming two daughters. Makinde made this disclosure during an interview with media personality Chude Jideonwo, where he spoke about his family, fatherhood and the decision to have a third child. Recounting how they planned their family, the governor said he initially wanted just one child but reluctantly agreed to have two after his wife questioned why they should have only one. According to him, he was comfortable with having two daughters and did not consider the gender of his children important. “Gender doesn’t mean anything to me because I felt whether a girl or a boy, it’s all linked up to how you’re going to bring them up and how you set them up to impact their environment, and you can do it with any kid,” he said. Makinde, however, explained that cultural expectations and comments from his mother-in-law amplified his wife’s desire to have a male child. He said his mother-in-law told his wife that Yoruba men whose wives did not give birth to boys could seek to have a male child outside their marriages. “I’m a Yoruba man, but I think I am okay with the girls that God has blessed us with,” he recalled saying. The governor disclosed that it took more than five years for him to understand his wife’s desire to have a son, after which they agreed to explore ways of having a male child. He said he subsequently purchased a book on how to conceive a boy, which they both read and followed, alongside purchasing ovulation kits. “So, I said, okay, well, that’s fine. We have to go and buy a book on how to have a boy, and then we’ll read it and apply strictly,” he said. Makinde added that their efforts eventually resulted in the birth of their son, who became their third child. “That was it. That was what produced the boy, and I was finally left off the hook,” he said. Vanguard News The post ‘I bought book on how to have boy-child’ – Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Driver Arrested Over Crash, Inferno That Killed 31 In Egypt
item.description: Egyptian prosecutors announced on Thursday the arrest of a man accused of causing a massive fire that erupted when a fuel tanker overturned on a packed highway in Cairo, killing 31 people . The prosecution said the man had “admitted” to speeding when his car collided with the tanker, “causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course”. When the car hit the truck, one of its tyres exploded, causing it to overturn, the prosecution said. The fire erupted as a result of a petrol leak, it added. This video grab taken from UGC images posted on social media on November 25, 2026, shows flames engulfing the area during a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate. Photo by – / VARIOUS SOURCES / AFP Footage from the scene showed a huge fireball and thick black smoke rising above the densely populated capital’s Al-Waraq neighbourhood as motorists on the ring road sounded their horns and struggled to get away. The prosecution said an investigation is underway to determine the driver’s criminal liability. The health ministry put the final toll at 31 dead and 21 wounded. More than 20 million people live in Greater Cairo, a sprawling and dense metropolis. With its informal residential areas and often dilapidated infrastructure, Egypt has suffered several deadly fires in recent years. Car crashes are common and often blamed on reckless driving, poor maintenance, and uneven law enforcement, with traffic laws also being widely flouted. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road accidents across the country, according to Egypt’s state statistics agency. Flames And Smoke In 2018, the government issued a decision banning heavy transport vehicles from accessing the ring road around Greater Cairo from 6:00 am to midnight. Emergency services personnel and bystanders gather beside the wreckage of a tanker truck following a fire in the Al-Waraq neighbourhood of Imbaba district, Giza Governorate, on November 25, 2026. Photo by MAHMOUD EL-KHAWAS / AFP Wednesday’s disaster occurred at around 7:00 pm — at a time when the road was packed with pedestrians, buses and cars. Traffic had returned to normal in the early hours of Thursday after rescue operations ended and the wreckage of the truck and burned-out cars was cleared. “We were driving on the flyover above the ring road and saw flames rising to a height I can’t even describe,” said Wagih Ragheb, a witness to the disaster. “Then the explosions started… We got out of the car and went down to the ring road and found a catastrophic situation: buses and cars completely charred, and many dead.” Footage posted online by passersby showed people pulling others out of their cars in the inferno that erupted after the truck overturned. “We have a problem with our roads. These accidents happen very often, and no one knows how to solve this,” said Abdel Rahman Ahmed, who was at a Cairo hospital to donate blood for the wounded. item.title: 74 Killed In Niger Communal Clash, Bago Orders Investigation, Donates N148m To Families
item.description: The clash between Kambari vigilantes and Fulani herders in Borgu Local Government Area of Niger State resulted in the death of 74 persons. The state’s governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, disclosed this during a visit to the Emir of Borgu, Alhaji Halilu Sani Dantoro, at his palace in New Bussa, the LGA’s headquarters. Terrorists had, last Saturday, attacked Lumman-Ba’are community in Borgu LGA, killing the village head, Mallam Bawa Muhammad, his wife and three of his children. They also set his palace ablaze. Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago, has ordered a thorough investigation into the clashes.‎ ‎The governor commiserated with the traditional ruler and people of the kingdom over the tragic incident. ‎Bago said the investigation was aimed at identifying those responsible for the violence and uncovering the remote and immediate causes of the recurring communal conflicts, with a view to preventing future occurrences. ‎He called on residents of the affected communities to embrace peaceful coexistence, tolerance and mutual understanding, stressing that no meaningful development could take place in an atmosphere of violence and hostility. ‎The governor expressed sympathy with the families of the victims and announced a donation of ₦2 million to each of the 74 affected families, amounting to ₦148 million, alongside the provision of foodstuffs and building materials to support those whose houses were destroyed during the clashes. ‎He commended the Borgu Emirate Council for its continued efforts towards maintaining peace and unity among the people, while urging Nigerians to learn to live together irrespective of their differences. ‎In his response, the Emir of Borgu, Muhammad Haliru -Dantoro Kitoro IV, appreciated the governor for the condolence visit and the timely deployment of security personnel to the area. ‎The traditional ruler acknowledged the state government’s efforts in deploying joint tactical security teams to tackle security challenges, including insurgency, in the area. He, however, expressed sadness that some individuals had chosen to resort to violence despite ongoing efforts by the government and security agencies to restore lasting peace. ‎The Emir also commended security agencies for their swift response, which he said helped to contain the situation and restore normalcy to the affected communities. ‎In his remarks, the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi, commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for his efforts towards addressing security challenges across the country, noting that the restructuring of the nation’s security architecture was yielding positive results. ‎He also praised Governor Bago for his commitment to tackling insecurity in parts of Niger State and acknowledged the contributions of security agencies in containing threats to lives and property. ‎The governor was accompanied on the visit by the Minister of State for Agriculture, Senator Sabi Abdullahi; Member representing Borgu/Agwara Federal Cons

item.title: Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations
item.description: ‎Niger State Governor, Umaru Bago, has received the report of the Judicial Commission of Inquiry established to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of 37 artisanal miners while in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger State Command. ‎The Governor received the report from the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, at the Government House, Minna, where he reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to implementing its recommendations. ‎Governor Bago expressed appreciation to the Commission on behalf of the bereaved families, the Miners Association and the NSCDC, describing the report as an important document that would guide stakeholders in addressing the circumstances surrounding the tragic incident. ‎He commended Justice Muhammad and members of the Commission for their dedication, sacrifices and thoroughness throughout the investigation, assuring that the government would carefully consider the findings and recommendations. ‎The Governor also disclosed that a copy of the report would be forwarded to the Presidency for reference, underscoring the importance of the investigation and its outcome. ‎Earlier, the Chairman of the Commission, Justice Muhammad Muhammad, thanked the Governor for the confidence reposed in the panel and the opportunity to serve. ‎He explained that the Commission received nine memoranda, conducted public hearings and carried out inspection visits to two mining sites, two NSCDC offices and the General Hospital in Minna as part of its investigation. ‎Justice Muhammad said the evidence and facts gathered during the proceedings formed the basis of the Commission’s findings and recommendations. ‎He further explained that the report was presented in three volumes for ease of reference, with Volume One containing the findings, observations and recommendations; Volume Two containing the records of proceedings; and Volume Three comprising all exhibits tendered before the Commission. ‎In his remarks, the Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Nasiru Mu’azu, described the deaths of the 37 artisanal miners as a grave incident in the history of Niger State. ‎He commended Governor Bago for demonstrating commitment to the rule of law by establishing the Judicial Commission of Inquiry to investigate the incident and ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were thoroughly examined. ‎Mu’azu assured that the Ministry of Justice would carefully study the report and advise the government on appropriate actions and the next steps to be taken. ‎ ‎ The post Gov Bago Receives Report On 37 Miners Deaths, Pledges Full Implementation Of Recommendations appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 2027: Violence, Intimidation, Use Of Thugs May Discourage Voters, Amupitan Warns Political Parties
item.description: The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, has condemned violence associated with political campaigns, warning political parties and their supporters against actions capable of threatening peace and undermining the electoral process. Amupitan warned on Thursday as ‎ the Commission and security agencies meet to strengthen election security ahead of the 2027 general election. ‎The INEC Chairman stressed the need for political actors to embrace issue-based campaigns, respect opposing views and conduct their political activities within the provisions of the law. Stressing that no political ambition is worth the blood of the citizens ‎He noted that political violence, intimidation and the use of thugs recently witnessed in some states during campaigns could discourage voter participation and weaken public confidence in the democratic process. ‎ Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, and National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, at the meeting. ‎Prof Amupitan said that the commission is working closely with the office of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, to identify flash points across the country. ‎He noted that election security remains a collective responsibility, requiring all relevant agencies to work together in addressing violence, intimidation and other activities capable of undermining the credibility of elections. Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Disu at the meeting ‎Amupitan further emphasised the need for security agencies to operate with professionalism, impartiality and respect for the rule of law, warning that no political interest should be allowed to compromise their constitutional responsibilities. ‎In attendance are the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, the Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, and the Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, among others. ‎The Inspector-General of Police, in his welcoming address, emphasised the need for improved collaboration, intelligence sharing and coordinated security operations to address potential threats to the electoral process. Director General of the State Security Service, Oluwatosin Ajayi, at the meeting. While giving an update on preparations for the upcoming general elections during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), on Wednesday, Amuipitan said that the Commission is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. According to him, INEC has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027.
